of The Hon'ble Mr. Justice Bipin Chander Negi, Judge Whether approved for reporting?

For the Petitioner rt : Mr. Romesh Verma, Senior Advocate with Mr. Sumit Sharma,
Advocate.

For the respondents : Ms. Anup Rattan, Advocate General with Ms. Seema Sharma,
Deputy Advocate General.
Bipin Chander Negi, Judge
In this writ petition, petitioner contends that he owns land in Khata No.112, Khatauni No.45, total measuring 00-29-58 hectares, situated at Mauja Dhara, Tehsil Rohru, District Shimla.

The petitioner further contend that through this land a road was laid in the year,
1996-97 known as Rohru-Dhara-Shekhal road.
Other than the aforesaid, petitioner has alleged that no acquisition proceedings were initiated, hence, no compensation was paid to the petitioner.
1 Whether reporters of Local Papers may be allowed to see the judgment?

2. The petitioner has further alleged that he had raised objections for laying of the road, but since an impression was given by the concerned respondents that he would be paid .
compensation, in accordance with law, petitioner had permitted laying of the road through his land.
Despite aforesaid assurance given, no compensation was ever paid to the petitioner.

The petitioner has further alleged that certain others, whose land was of utilized for the said road, had been paid compensation vide Award Nos. 88/2008, 33/2008, 58/2008, 47/2008, 8/2010, 58/2011, rt 26/2011 and 50/2010, passed by the Land Acquisition Collector, HPPWD, South Zone, Winter Field, Shimla, on 3.10.2008, 23.10.2008, 30.11.2011, 3.0.2008, 20.4.2010, 30.11.2011, 17.10.2010 and 24.08.2011, respectively.
3. Petitioner had issued a Demand Notice through registered post on 10.12.2021 requesting the respondents to acquire the land and make payment of compensation.

In furtherance thereof nothing Bish Ram vs State Of Himachal Pradesh And Another on 13 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192864456/

sentences.text: 4. In response to the petition, the respondent/State has taken a stand that the petitioner in question had voluntarily offered his land for availing road connectivity.
The road in question was constructed with the verbal consent of the petitioner.
Besides the aforesaid, the respondents have contended that the petitioner post availing the road connectivity is unjustified in raising a demand for compensation.

Other than the aforesaid, the plea of the disputed question of fact and laches has also been raised by .
the respondents.
The contentions of both the parties have been noted.

5. From the facts narrated above, it is clear that the respondents have utilized the land of the petitioner for the of construction of road without initiating any proceedings for acquisition of the same and without having any evidence of rt consent of the petitioner qua the same.

6. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner has placed reliance on the decision of the Hon'ble Division Bench of this Court in CWP No.6581 of 2021, titled Labdhu Ram vs. State of H.P. &
Others, dated 28.06.2023.

entities.text:
Labdhu Ram vs. State of H.P. &
Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In my considered opinion, the aforesaid authoritative pronouncement squarely covers the case of the present petitioner.

7. In view of the above settled legal position, I am of the opinion that the stand of the respondent/State that it need not pay any compensation for utilizing the petitioner's land for the purpose of laying a road cannot be countenanced and the respondent/ State is bound to pay the compensation at the rate of market value to the petitioner for utilizing his land for the purpose of the road.

8. Therefore, the writ petition is allowed with costs of .
Rs.10,000/- and a direction is issued to the respondents to demarcate the land of the petitioner utilized for the purpose of the road in question within four weeks, treat it as having been acquired for the said purpose and pay him the highest amount of towards compensation among compensation under the Awards with all statutory benefits under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 rt within eight weeks.

Pending miscellaneous application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed of.
 ( Bipin Chander Negi)
